text: General Vandenberg was a nephew of the late, great Republican Senator Arthur Vandenberg,
and like the Senator, was a victim of cancer.
Both of them had all the treatments that conventional medicine could offer.
General Vandenberg directed the creation and operation of the Air Force during World War II,
shaping it into the tremendous force for victory,
the victory in which it played such an important part.
A likable, handsome, and brilliant leader,
he never gave up his struggle to keep America safe by keeping the Air Force strong.
Millions of Americans will remember him best
as the result of a picture that was widely published,
a picture that was taken during a Senate committee hearing last year.
It showed General Vandenberg with his head buried in his arms on the table,
He was a very sick man even then.
